> [!WARNING]
>
> The generation routes consu
me **no customer credits** (the model cost is on\n> MCPJam). They are still subject to usage limits, and each limit means a\n> dif
ferent wait: a per-minute burst brake (`429`, retry in seconds), your\n> organization's daily generation quota (`429`, resets at U
TC midnight), and\n> MCPJam's own daily budget for the feature (`429` with\n> `details.code: \"platform_capacity\"`, resets at UTC
midnight). All three carry\n> `Retry-After`. Honor it rather than guessing. `details.canTopUp` is `false`\n> on every one: buying

credits does not lift them, so do not retry in a loop
> or switch identities to get around them.

**Swarms, runs** (`/projects

/{projectId}/goals/{goalId}/runs`,
`.../goal-runs/...`): launching a goal and reading what it produced:

| Endpoint | What it d

oes |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | That goal's runs, newest first |
| `POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | **Launch.
** Answers `202`; the fan-out has started, not finished. Send `Idempotency-Key`. Optional `expectedSponsored` is how many conversa
tions you expect MCPJam to sponsor; a different actual split is a `409` (`details.code: swarm_funding_changed`) and nothing is cre
ated. The response can report `funding` (`sponsored`, `credits`, `total`) |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}` | The full run: counts,
per-target breakdown, per-session `attempts` |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/sessions` | The chat sessions the run produced (summ
aries, not transcripts) |\n| `POST .../goal-runs/{runId}/cancel` | Stop a run. Idempotent; a second cancel is `200` with `alreadyC

anceled: true`, not a `409` |

Three things worth knowing before you write the client:

* **Always send `Idempotency-Key` on a
launch.** It spends model credits, so a\n retry of a dropped response must not run the goal twice. Replaying a key\n returns th
e original run with `deduped: true` and starts no second runner\n and consumes no quota. Omitting the header is read as a request
that declined\n to identify itself, and gets a fresh run every time.\n* **Check `canceled` before reporting a failure.** A stopp
ed run carries\n `status: \"failed\"`, because cancellation is recorded as a marker rather than\n a status of its own. `stale: t
rue` is the third case: the runner went silent\n and the watchdog settled the run.\n* **`targetId`, not `hostId`, identifies a ta
rget.** Two environments can\n resolve to the same host with different servers, so a run can hold two\n targets that share a `ho

stId`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Launching **spends**: a run fans out into `targets × iterations`
> sessions. Two different `429`s ca
n come back; the per-minute burst brake\n> (retry in seconds) and your plan's daily launch cap (resets at UTC midnight).\n> Both n
ormally carry `Retry-After`; back off on your own when one does not.\n\n**Swarms, insights**: what a run revealed. Read these in o
rder of cost: the\nroll-up and the scorecard are deterministic and free, the findings registry\naggregates them, and swarm run ins

ights run a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals-overview` | Project roll-up: recent runs, goal-comp
letion rates, repeat failures, trend |\n| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/scorecard` | One run's deterministic rubric result. No model,
no spend |\n| `GET .../goal-findings` | Criteria that keep failing, tracked across swarm runs |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findi
ngId}/dismiss` | Hide a finding |\n| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Un-hide it |\n| `GET .../swarm-runs/{swarmRu
nId}/insights` | Poll a swarm run's generated insights. **404 = nobody asked** |\n| `POST .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` |
Request them. `202`; scheduled, not done |\n| `DELETE .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Cancel a generation still `pending`

|

Two arithmetic traps worth naming, because both produce numbers that look
plausible and are wrong:

* **Divide by `session
sGraded`, never by the session total.** Three failures\n out of four graded sessions, in a run that attempted forty, is 75%, not\
n 7.5%.\n* **`failedGradingCount` is not `failCount`.** A crashed judge is not a\n regression, and folding the two together make

s one look like the other.

And one modelling note: a finding's `status` is a lifecycle:
`new | recurring | regressed | resolve
d`. `dismissed` is *not* one of them.\nDismissal is the orthogonal `dismissedAt`, so a finding can be both recurring\nand dismisse

d, and hiding one never claims it stopped happening.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting swarm run insights consumes **no credits**;
the model cost is on\n> MCPJam. It still counts against the `insightsPerDay` ledger, which counts\n> REQUESTS and is **shared** wi
th eval-run and user-testing insights, so a\n> request here takes one from there too. Poll the `GET` rather than\n> re-requesting;
`force: true` deliberately takes a second slice.\n>\n> Three refusals, three different meanings: a short `429` is the per-minute\
n> brake (wait seconds), a `429` naming `insightsPerDay` is the daily ledger\n> (its `Retry-After`, when present, counts to UTC mi

dnight), and a `403` means
> the feature is not available to your organization; waiting will never help.

**User testing** (`/p
rojects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/study`,\n`.../studies/...`): publishing an environment for real visitors, reading
what\nthey did, and controlling who can reach it. A **study** is a published\nenvironment: one per environment, addressed by its

own id once it exists.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `PUT .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Publish.** Id
empotent: republishing returns the existing study, and `created: false` says so. Project **admin** |\n| `DELETE .../environments/{
environmentId}/study` | **Unpublish.** The link dies and live sessions end. `deleted: false` when there was nothing published |\n|
`PATCH .../studies/{studyId}` | Rename, re-describe, or change `mode` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions` | What visitors d
id: one row per session, with feedback and a first-message preview |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions/{sessionId}` | One ses
sion's transcript, paged. Tool payloads and blobs are dropped |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/guest-execution` | The spend dial fo
r anonymous visitors: daily credits, computer starts, concurrency |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rotate-link` | **Mint a new sha
re link.** No body; the new secret is minted server-side |\n| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/members` | Invite someone (or change thei
r role) on an `invited_only` study |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/members/{memberIdOrEmail}` | Remove someone. Their grant is
revoked, ending their live sessions |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point the study at a different environment in the s

ame project |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Rotating the link does not evict anyone who already used it.** It stops the
> old URL from
granting NEW access; the grants already redeemed under it stay\n> valid. That is the single most important thing to know here, bec
ause rotation\n> is what you reach for when a link leaks, and on its own it does not undo the\n> leak. Rotate *and* remove the mem

bers you did not intend to have.
>
> What DOES take effect at once, ending live sessions rather than waiting for
> expiry: unpu
